subject.title: [Feature]: Mobile apps: per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies

question: Should OpenClaw mobile apps support arbitrary per-gateway proxy headers as proposed, or should the mobile contract be narrowed to typed proxy-auth schemes before the iOS and Android PRs land?
rationale: This is not a routine source fix: the feature stores and replays credentials before Gateway authentication, changes mobile settings/storage surfaces, and must define what headers are allowed and where they may be sent.

options.title: Review and land split platform PRs
options.body: Proceed with the iOS and Android PRs only after owner/security review confirms the shared arbitrary-header contract and real behavior proof are sufficient.

options.title: Narrow to typed proxy auth first
options.body: Ask the platform PRs to support a smaller Basic/Bearer/fixed-token contract before considering arbitrary header name/value pairs.

options.title: Defer mobile proxy headers
options.body: Keep mobile reverse-proxy header injection unsupported for now and document VPN/Tailscale/proxy-bypass alternatives while the security model remains unsettled.

recommendation.title: Review and land split platform PRs
recommendation.body: Proceed with the iOS and Android PRs only after owner/security review confirms the shared arbitrary-header contract and real behavior proof are sufficient.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter authored the issue, opened the platform implementation PRs, and has the strongest recent signal across mobile gateway auth and product/security boundary work.
